Inside the `isr()` function, we set a flag `i2cTransmissionInProgress` to true to indicate that an I2C transmission is in progress. In the `loop()` function, we check if the `i2cTransmissionInProgress` flag is true. If it is, we run a routine (in this case, just printing a message to the serial monitor) and then reset the flag to false. You can modify the routine as per your requirements. Make sure to replace `INTERRUPT_PIN` with the pin number you want to use for the interrupt. Also, adjust the `Wire.begin()` statement with the desired SDA and SCL pin numbers. Note: Be cautious when using `Serial.println()` inside an interrupt service routine, as it can interfere with other time-critical tasks. LLM: Certainly! Let's dive into what MTCNN and FaceNet are, and then provide examples of how to use them effectively. ### What is MTCNN? MTCNN (Multi-Task Cascaded Convolutional Networks) is a powerful face detection and alignment algorithm. It splits the face detection task into three stages: 1. **Proposal Network (P-Net)**: Quickly proposes candidate windows that might contain faces. 2. **Refine Network (R-Net)**: Refines these candidate windows to remove unlikely ones, thereby reducing the number of windows. 3. **Output Network (O-Net)**: Further refines the candidates and outputs the final bounding boxes, keypoints, and alignment results. ### What is FaceNet? LLM: ### Overview The Online Time Deposit project, initiated in 2020 within the Hogan platform, introduced a New Fund calculation engine. Its purpose is to monitor and incentivize customers who make new deposits through online or mobile banking by offering higher interest rates. New funds are tracked for up to five working days using specific transaction codes, allowing the bank to effectively manage incentives. ### Proposed Process As part of an upgrade, Atlas will implement a similar feature with improved controls to track new funds arrival. Below is an outline of the components and functionality proposed for the New Funds tracking in Atlas. #### 2.1 New Fund Definition **Tracking Criteria:** - Customer segments will drive tracking mechanisms. - Only credit transactions from the following sources will qualify as new funds: - Outside the bank - Cash - Cheque - Cashier Order - Bank Transfers (CHATs, TT, FPS) - Redemption from Investment Products - ELI - Debt Securities (Bonds & Structured Products) - Insurance - Securities - Unit Trust - FX Conversion - e.g., Converting from HKD to USD is treated as new funds. **Calculation Metrics:** 1. **Total New Funds** = Sum of new funds from the current day and the last four business days, identified through specific transaction types/codes. 2. **Utilized Funds** = Funds used for deposits from digital channels, tracked similarly over the same time frame. 3. **Available New Funds** = Total New Funds - Utilized Funds **Account Level Tracking:** Funds will be consolidated at the customer level, considering primary account holders while being categorized by currency. New funds are recorded at the account level and aggregated at the customer level. Notably, reversals and backdated transactions won't be considered. **Transaction Identification:** All transactions in Atlas can be identified with specific transaction codes. Existing statistical group features for tracking incoming credits will be leveraged for the New Funds Engine. A special emphasis on certain transactions might require tracking via statistical groups, which can be achieved by defining and mapping transaction codes accordingly. #### 2.2 New Fund Definition Parameter This section serves to define which segments are eligible for new funds tracking. **Attributes:** - **Statistical Group Code**: To identify incoming funds. - **New Fund Definition Days**: Number of days for tracking new funds. - **History Tracking Days**: Days for historical tracking of new fund entries. - **Segment Code**: Defines the segment for which new funds are tracked. **Primary Keys:** - **Parent Table**: Statistical Group Code - **Child Table**: - Statistical Group Code - Segment Code **Tables to be Created:** - `NFNDDAYS` - `NFNDDAYSDT` #### 2.3 New Fund Definition Parameter Enquiry This will serve as the inquiry mechanism for the New Funds Parameter screen. **Input Parameter:** - Segment Code #### 2.4 NTB Definition in Atlas The logic for determining if a customer qualifies as a New-to-Bank (NTB) or Existing-to-Bank (ETB) customer is proposed as follows: **Criteria:** - Oldest CASA Account opening date: Current system date - 60 days. - Relationship ID open date: Current system date - 365 days. The system will use parameterized values to calculate and validate the NTB or ETB status of customers based on these criteria. --- This document provides a detailed guideline for implementing the New Funds tracking functionality in Atlas, ensuring best practices are followed and relevant stakeholder requirements are met.

LLM: ### 2.5 Customer Level Fund Tracking #### 2.5.1 New Service to Update Incoming New Funds Online The goal of this section is to create a new table for tracking incoming new funds online for each customer. Here’s how it works: 1. **Creation of a New Table**: - A new database table will be created to keep track of incoming new funds for customers. 2. **Asynchronous Updates**: - This table will be updated asynchronously, meaning it will automatically update based on incoming transactions without needing manual intervention. 3. **Tracking Duration**: - The duration for which transactions are tracked will be determined by parameters set in the system. - For example, if the defined tracking period is five days, any eligible credit transaction will be tracked for those five days. 4. **Historical Records**: - Once a transaction exceeds the defined tracking period, it will be moved to a different table called the "history table". - This history table will maintain records for a specified number of days (defined by system parameters) for reference. 5. **Contribution to New Funds Balance**: - Each eligible credit transaction will be added to the customer’s new funds available balance. This means that when new funds come in, they will be counted towards how much new funds a customer has available for creating a Time Deposit (TD). 6. **Tracking Utilization**: - The table will also keep track of if any new funds are used (utilized) to create Time Deposits or if funds are withdrawn (which would reduce their available new funds). 7. **Enquiry Screen**: - A new enquiry screen will be developed to allow users to view their day-wise new funds and available new funds based on their customer ID. 8. **Joint Accounts**: - In cases where an account is jointly owned, any new funds calculated will be credited towards the primary account holder’s available funds. 9. **Account Level Calculation**: - It’s important to note that while some master records exist between relationships and accounts in Atlas, the new fund calculation will be performed only at the customer level, not at the individual account level. **Example Explanation:** Let’s take a simple example to illustrate the tracking of new funds: - Suppose a customer with ID `R1` has two accounts: - **Account A1**: - Has new funds of HKD 8,000, with a total balance of HKD 10,000. - **Account A2**: - Has new funds of HKD 2,000, with a total balance of HKD 5,000. **Total New Funds Calculation for the Customer**: - Total New Funds = HKD 8,000 (from A1) + HKD 2,000 (from A2) = HKD 10,000.
